clues.clue: This Windows 10 edition is recommended for business use and includes domain connectivity.
clues.explain: Windows 10 Pro adds business features Home lacks -- domain join, Group Policy, BitLocker, and Remote Desktop host -- making it the standard business edition.

clues.clue: This Windows 8.1 edition cannot use BitLocker drive encryption.
clues.explain: The base Windows 8.1 (Core) edition omits BitLocker; you needed Pro or Enterprise for full-disk encryption.

clues.clue: This feature is NOT available in any Windows Home edition.
clues.explain: Encrypting File System (per-file encryption) is absent from all Home editions; it requires Pro/Enterprise, unlike BitLocker which encrypts the whole volume.

clues.clue: BitLocker encryption keys are stored in this hardware component.
clues.explain: BitLocker seals its volume keys in the TPM, a tamper-resistant chip that releases them only if boot-integrity checks pass, so a stolen drive can't be read elsewhere.

clues.clue: This group exists in Windows 7+ only for backward compatibility with legacy applications.
clues.response: What is the Power Users Group?
clues.explain: The Power Users group survives only for backward compatibility with legacy apps; it no longer grants the elevated rights it did back in Windows XP.

clues.clue: This command is used to change directories in the command prompt.
clues.explain: cd (change directory) moves your prompt's working location; cd .. goes up one level, and cd %USERPROFILE% returns to your home folder.

clues.clue: This command verifies and restores corrupted Windows system files.
clues.explain: System File Checker scans protected OS files and restores corrupted ones from a cached known-good copy -- a first fix for system instability.

clues.clue: This command locates and repairs disk errors.
clues.explain: chkdsk /r locates bad sectors and recovers readable data (it implies /f to fix errors); it usually needs a reboot to lock the system volume.

clues.clue: This command completely wipes a hard drive including the partitioning system.
clues.explain: diskpart is the scriptable disk/partition manager; its 'clean' command erases the partition table entirely, so it's used to fully repurpose a drive.

clues.clue: This switch with the dir command displays all files in subdirectories.
clues.explain: dir /s recurses into every subdirectory, listing files across the whole tree rather than just the current folder.

clues.clue: This should be disabled to prevent potentially harmful programs from automatically running from removable media.
clues.explain: AutoRun auto-executes a program from inserted media; disabling it blocks a classic USB/CD malware vector (the autorun.inf trick).

clues.clue: This policy is the best defense against brute force attacks on local passwords.
clues.explain: Locking an account after N failed attempts defeats online brute-force guessing by capping tries; password complexity alone doesn't stop rapid attempts.

clues.clue: This authentication method uses user ID, password, and a unique PIN sent via text.
clues.explain: Multi-factor authentication combines categories (a password plus a texted PIN), so a stolen password alone can't log in -- the texted code is 'something you have'.

clues.clue: Resetting a local user password causes loss of access to files encrypted with this.
clues.explain: EFS file keys are tied to the user's credentials; an admin resetting (rather than the user changing) the password can orphan those keys and lock the encrypted files.

clues.clue: This wireless security feature allows only specific device addresses to connect to the network.
clues.explain: MAC filtering admits only listed hardware addresses to the network; it's a weak control (MACs are easily spoofed) but limits casual connections.

clues.clue: Open this tool and end the process to fix an application that's not responding.
clues.explain: Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) lets you End Task on a hung application without rebooting the whole machine.

clues.clue: This is the first troubleshooting step after Startup Repair fails on a boot issue.
clues.explain: Safe Mode boots Windows with minimal drivers/services; if Startup Repair fails, it's the next step to reach a working desktop and undo the cause.

clues.clue: If an app works in Safe Mode but not normal mode, this is causing the issue.
clues.response: What is the operating system or a driver?
clues.explain: If a fault disappears in Safe Mode (which loads minimal drivers), the culprit is a third-party driver or service that only loads in normal mode.

clues.clue: When a mobile device performs slowly after an hour, do this first.
clues.response: What is close or disable all unused running apps?
clues.explain: Background apps drain CPU, RAM, and battery; closing them is the first, cheapest fix for a phone slowing down before more drastic steps.

clues.clue: This Windows feature runs before the OS starts to scan when malware prevents access even in Safe Mode.
clues.response: What is Windows Defender Offline Scan?
clues.explain: Defender Offline reboots into a minimal environment and scans before Windows loads, removing rootkits/persistent malware that hide once the OS (even Safe Mode) is running.

clues.clue: This partitioning scheme is limited to approximately 2 TB volumes.
clues.explain: MBR's 32-bit addressing caps usable disks at ~2 TB and allows only four primary partitions; GPT removes both limits.

clues.clue: This file system is recommended for internal Windows boot drives.
clues.explain: NTFS is required for a Windows boot volume; it adds journaling, ACL permissions, encryption, and large-file support that FAT32/exFAT lack.

clues.clue: This modern partitioning standard supports drives larger than 2 TB.
clues.explain: GPT uses 64-bit addressing for drives far beyond 2 TB and many partitions, and pairs with UEFI firmware (versus MBR+legacy BIOS).

clues.clue: Windows automatically performs this maintenance task once a week.
clues.response: What is defragmentation (or TRIM for SSDs)?
clues.explain: Windows auto-optimizes weekly: defragmenting HDDs to make files contiguous, but issuing TRIM on SSDs instead -- SSDs must not be defragmented.

clues.clue: A partition that has been formatted with a file system and assigned a drive letter is called this.
clues.explain: A volume is a partition that's been formatted with a filesystem and given a drive letter or mount point -- the usable storage unit the OS presents.

clues.clue: This short-range wireless technology is used for mobile payments at retail checkout.
clues.explain: NFC works only at a few centimeters, which is exactly why it's used for tap-to-pay -- the short range is a built-in security feature.

clues.clue: This mobile feature allows other devices to connect to the Internet through cellular data.
clues.explain: A mobile hotspot shares the phone's cellular data over Wi-Fi (or USB/Bluetooth tethering) so other devices get Internet.

clues.clue: Touching wrong icons on a mobile device is often caused by this accessory interfering.
clues.explain: A poorly fitted or thick screen protector can throw off touch registration, causing mis-taps -- check it before assuming a digitizer fault.

clues.clue: Before performing a factory reset, always do this first.
clues.response: What is back up all user data?
clues.explain: A factory reset erases everything, so backing up contacts, photos, and app data first is mandatory before the wipe.

clues.clue: This AAA service is a Cisco-based upgrade to RADIUS for enhanced network security.
clues.explain: TACACS+ is Cisco's AAA protocol that, unlike RADIUS, encrypts the entire payload and separates authentication, authorization, and accounting -- favored for device administration.
